stemMd: A crate slides from rest down a smooth (frictionless) ramp that is 10 m long and inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Take g = 10 m/s². What is the speed of the crate at the bottom of the ramp?
explanationMd:
With no friction, mechanical energy is conserved: the potential energy lost equals the kinetic energy gained, $mgh = \tfrac12 mv^{2}$. The mass cancels.

**The height.** Only the vertical drop counts, not the length along the slope: $h = L\sin30^{\circ} = 10\times\tfrac12 = 5\ \text{m}$.

**The speed.** $v^{2} = 2gh = 2\times10\times5 = 100$, so $v = 10\ \text{m/s}$.

**Check with kinematics.** Along the slope the acceleration is $g\sin30^{\circ} = 5\ \text{m/s}^2$. Starting from rest, $v^{2} = 2aL = 2\times5\times10 = 100$, so again $v = 10\ \text{m/s}$.

distractorRationale.b: Quotes the acceleration along the slope, $g\sin30^{\circ} = 5\ \text{m/s}^2$, as if it were the speed. An acceleration has units of m/s², and the speed comes from $v^{2} = 2aL$.
distractorRationale.e: Loses the factor 2 in the energy balance, writing $v^{2} = gh = 50$ instead of $v^{2} = 2gh$. From $mgh = \tfrac12 mv^{2}$ the 2 must appear.
distractorRationale.d: Uses the whole 10 m length of the ramp as the height, ignoring the 30° angle. Only the vertical drop of 5 m changes the potential energy.
distractorRationale.c: Stops at $v^{2} = 2gh = 100$ and quotes that as the speed, without taking the square root.

accessibilityText: A work and energy question. A crate slides from rest down a smooth, frictionless ramp that is 10 metres long and inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Use g equal to 10 metres per second squared. The speed at the bottom is wanted. The choices are 5 metres per second, 5 times the square root of 2 metres per second, 10 metres per second, 10 times the square root of 2 metres per second, and 100 metres per second.

provenance.notes: Original item. sin 30 degrees is exactly one half so the arithmetic is exact. Wrong choices: acceleration quoted as speed, a lost factor of 2, the ramp length used as the height, and v squared not square-rooted.

review.author: polito-til-i-wave6-physics-technical-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: h = 10 sin30 = 5 m; v = sqrt(2*10*5) = 10 m/s. 10√2 m/s comes from using the full 10 m length as the height, and 5√2 m/s and 5 m/s are other slips. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tili-phys-tech-run9) reached the same answer: Vertical drop h=10 sin30=5 m; v=sqrt(2gh)=sqrt(100)=10 m/s. 10*sqrt2 uses full length as height; 5*sqrt2 and 5 are halving errors; 100 is v^2.]
